# Agent integration contract (`/ziki`)

Phase 4 adds a shared skill and slash-command files so a coding agent can run
the repository workflow: inspect → plan → human approval → work → verify →
review → present. The files are generated by `ziki init` and recorded in
`ziki.json#managedFiles`.

## Generated files

| Path | Harness | Frontmatter |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/ziki/SKILL.md` | Claude Code, and OpenCode (shared skills directory) | `name`, `description` only |
| `.claude/commands/ziki.md` | Claude Code slash command `/ziki` | `description` only |
| `.opencode/commands/ziki.md` | OpenCode slash command `/ziki` | `description` only |

Detection also recognizes OpenCode's singular `.opencode/command/<name>.md`
where an existing install uses it (OD-08). `init` never writes the singular
path: it always emits the documented plural `commands/` directory.

The frontmatter fields are the minimal documented ones. No `agent`, `model`,
`allowed-tools`, or other harness-specific keys are used, so the files stay
valid in both harnesses.

## The fixed workflow

Every generated file carries the same seven steps:

1. **Inspect** — run `status`; read branch, divergence, worktree counts, last
   commit, detected agent files, and detected checks.
2. **Plan** — run `init` when `ziki.json` is missing or stale; show the plan
   to the human; a plan is not done work.
3. **Human approval** — get an explicit yes in the conversation before
   `init --apply`; only then may an agent pass `--yes` (an agent session is
   not an interactive terminal). Existing/changed files additionally need
   `--confirm <path>` per file.
4. **Work** — the agent implements; Ziki has no code-generation step.
5. **Verify** — the agent runs the project's own checks and reports real
   commands, exit codes, and failures. Detected checks are suggestions; a
   check that did not run is reported as not run.
6. **Review** — run `review` (read-only). Fix what it surfaces before claiming
   completion. The secret scan is a best-effort warning pass, not proof.
7. **Present decisions** — summarize changes, verified results, review
   findings, and open decisions. An `observed` check state means a record in
   `ziki.json` claims a result; it is quoted as recorded, never as verified by
   Ziki.

## CLI invocation and the name collision

The templates never call a bare `ziki` command. On some machines `ziki` is an
unrelated **Ziki bounty platform** CLI (installed as `~/.ziki/bin/ziki` and on
`PATH`), and the bounty platform also installs user-level `ziki` skills and
`/ziki` commands for Claude Code and OpenCode. The templates therefore always
instruct:

```text
node <ziki-cli>/bin/ziki.js <command> [options]
```

`<ziki-cli>` is a placeholder for this checkout's path; the skill tells the
agent to ask the human if it does not know it. No absolute paths are embedded,
so the generated files are byte-identical on every machine and reruns are
stable.

Name resolution cuts against the project-level files when both names exist.
Claude Code resolves a personal (user-level) skill before a project skill with
the same name, and OpenCode de-duplicates skill names across its search
locations; OpenCode's documentation also asks that skill names be unique
across locations. So on a machine where the bounty platform's user-level
`ziki` skill is installed, the project-level `ziki` skill is shadowed: `/ziki`
runs the bounty skill, not this workflow. A live probe on 2026-10-28 in a
repository generated by `init` confirmed exactly that in OpenCode. On a machine
without a conflicting `ziki` skill, the generated project skill and command
load normally. The skill description states explicitly that it is the
ziki-cli repository workflow, not the bounty platform.

## Verification status

- Static contract tests (`tests/unit/templates.test.js`,
  `tests/integration/harness-contract.test.js`) prove: documented paths,
  minimal frontmatter, skill name matches its directory, no absolute paths, no
  writes outside the repository, plural directory output.
- `init` behavior is covered by `tests/integration/init.test.js`: plan/apply,
  per-file confirmation, modified-since-recorded detection, recovery, and
  symlink/directory refusal.
- Loading the files in live Claude Code and OpenCode sessions is a manual
  acceptance check (AC-P4-01/02); it is not part of the automated suite
  because it requires interactive harness credentials and network access.
